answer.rationale:
The expiring, non-auto-renewing primary contract is the binding constraint: whatever I do must cover supply past day 85, which rules out add_second_source and defer_decision as standalone answers, and memory_c4's negotiation play is already foreclosed because the incumbent has refused to reopen price. That leaves renew (misses the 18% mandate) or move primary volume to the low-cost vendor (meets the mandate on price alone). So I intend to switch, but staged: award the low-cost vendor a guarded initial tranche with the incumbent retained on a short bridge/spot arrangement for the balance, rather than a clean cutover of 100% of volume in 14 days at 94% utilization with no buffer.

Verification targets are the two memories actually load-bearing for that call. memory_c2 is the sole basis for believing the low-cost vendor can carry primary volume, and its framing is suspiciously narrow: it praises unit cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy, and says nothing about on-time delivery, quality escapes, or what share of volume they actually carried. If the archived record shows they were a secondary or low-volume award, the mandate-meeting quote is not evidence of primary-scale capability and the tranche must be small. memory_c1 is the mirror: its 'no migration work' phrasing implies migration is non-trivial when it does occur, and I need the original record to size the cutover effort and qualification lead time against a 14-day clock.

Risk I am explicitly flagging: this cycle's decision sets the default for future cycles. A cost-driven switch that is later judged only on realized unit price will quietly re-weight this organization's memory toward price and away from continuity and allocation security — the very lessons memory_c3 and memory_c1 encode. I want the guarded tranche recorded with delivery-performance and quality metrics attached, not just savings, so the next agent inherits a two-sided record. If verification shows the low-cost vendor was never proven above a small volume share, I will shrink the tranche further and buy a short incumbent bridge instead of a full switch, accepting partial mandate attainment this cycle over a stockout at zero buffer. Dual-sourcing per memory_c3 remains the intended end state, deferred to the next review by the one-decision limit.
